The Challenge

Every receipt was in there, in a thousand different files

When a distribution company pays its transmission charges, POWERGRID issues a disbursement advice showing how the payment is split between licensees. To reconcile receipts for its transmission assets, IndiGrid needed every advice in one table.

1,000+ files

The advices sat in batch folders from DA 3011 to DA 4001. Opening each file and copying its rows would take weeks.

Unstructured data

Headers wrapped across lines, page footers and total rows sat inside tables, and numbers mixed Indian and Western commas.

The format kept changing

Later batches arrived as Excel instead of PDF, with title rows, serial dates and renamed licensees. Any fixed template would break.

Reconciliation needs every row

Billing, disbursement ratio, rebate, TDS and net disbursement all had to tie out, file by file, payer by payer.

HMC Approach

Teach Power Query to read an advice, then point it at the folder

Built with IndiGrid's finance team, in the Excel workbook they already used for reconciliation.

Select a step to see what happened.

Discover · Catalogue the mess

We sampled advices from every batch folder and listed every way they differed.

  • Two tables per advice: payment header and licensee-wise details.
  • Seven kinds of variation, from wrapped headers to Excel serial dates.
  • A format change from PDF to Excel partway through the series.

Deliverable: Variability catalogue and target schema.

Design · One schema, many inputs

Every file, whatever its format, ends up in the same twelve columns.

  • Advice number, date, payer, bill month, licensee and UTR.
  • Billing, ratio, gross realisation, rebate, TDS and net disbursement.
  • A check that ratio × RTGS amount matches gross realisation.

Deliverable: Canonical schema and validation rules.

Build · Custom functions

Each kind of variation got its own small, reusable M function.

  • fxTransformDA reads one file and routes PDF or Excel.
  • fxCleanHeaders, fxParseINR, fxSplitRTGS, fxMapLicensee, fxFromExcel.
  • A folder query that applies them to every file and stacks the results.

Deliverable: Power Query workbook with six custom functions.

Adopt · Drop files, press Refresh

The finance team's whole routine became two actions.

  • Save new advices into the batch folder.
  • Refresh: every file is read, cleaned and checked.
  • Any row failing a check is listed with its source file name.

Deliverable: One-page guide and walkthrough.

Scale · Ready for the next format

A new variation means one new mapping or function, not a rebuild.

  • Licensee name map kept in an Excel table the team edits.
  • New folders picked up automatically.
  • Output feeds receivables, TDS and rebate reconciliations.

Deliverable: Maintenance notes and mapping tables.

    Key Takeaways

    What any finance team can borrow

    01

    Solve one file, then the folder

    Once Power Query can read one advice reliably, a thousand is just a refresh.

    02

    Name every variation

    A catalogue of the ways files differ became a set of small functions. Each new quirk is one more rule, not a rebuild.

    03

    Check as you load

    Validation built into the query means reconciliation starts from data the team already trusts.
